هَدٌّ A weak man; (As, S, L, K;) i. e., weak in body; (L;) as also ↓ هِدٌّ : (K:) or, accord. to IAar, the latter only, meaning cowardly and weak: (S, L:) or هَدٌّ (Sh, L) and ↓ أَهدُّ (L, K) and ↓ هَدَادَةٌ (Sh, L, K) signify a cowardly (and weak, TA) man: (Sh, L, K:) and ↓ قَوْمٌ هَدَادٌ a cowardly people: (Sh, L:) pl. of هَدٌّ, ??: (L, K:) it has no broken pl. (L:) and of هِدٌّ, هِدّٰونَ. (K.) A man says to another, in threatening him, إِنِّى لَعَيْرُ هَدٍّ Verily I am not weak. (S, L.) ―
-b2- هَدٌّ Extreme odd age; decrepitude. (K, TA.) See 1. ＝
-A2- هَدٌّ A cough, or harsh, sound; as also ↓ هَدَدٌ . (L, K.) ―
-b2- هَدٌّ The braying of a camel. (Lh, L, K.) See 1. ＝
-A3- هَدٌّ A generous, liberal. beautiful man. (IAar. S, L, K. *) ―
-b2- A strong man. (IAar. L.) ―
-b3- لِى صَاحِبٌ هَدُّكَ صَاحِبًا, and مَرَرْتُ بِرَجُلٍ هَدِّكَ مِنْ رَجُلٍ: see 1.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
